translations.text: Listen! I will tell the best of dreams, which I dreamed in the middle of the night, when those who have speech were resting.
It seemed to me that I saw a most wondrous tree lifted into the air, wound about with light, the brightest of beams. That whole sign was covered with gold.
Gems stood fair at the corners of the earth, and there were five of them as well, up on the crossbeam. All the angels of the Lord gazed on it there, fair through all creation ordained.
That was certainly no criminal's gallows. Holy spirits gazed on it there, people across the earth, and all this glorious creation.

Wondrous was the tree of victory, and I was stained with sins, badly wounded with faults. I saw the tree of glory, honored with garments, shining with joys, adorned with gold; gems had covered the Ruler's tree in a worthy way.
Yet through that gold I could make out the ancient struggle of wretched ones, how it first began to bleed on the right side. I was all troubled with sorrows; I was afraid at that fair sight.
I saw that eager sign change its coverings and colors: at times it was drenched with moisture, soaked with the flow of blood, at times adorned with treasure.
Yet I, lying there a long while, gazed in sorrow at the Savior's tree, until I heard that it spoke.
Then the best of wood began to speak words: "It was long ago (I still remember it) that I was cut down at the edge of the forest, removed from my trunk.
Strong enemies seized me there, made me into a spectacle for themselves there, ordered me to lift up their criminals.

Men carried me there on their shoulders until they set me up on a hill. Plenty of enemies fastened me there. Then I saw the Lord of mankind hurrying with great courage, because he meant to climb up on me.
There I did not dare, against the Lord's word, to bend or break, when I saw the surface of the earth tremble. I could have struck down all the enemies, yet I stood fast.
Then the young hero stripped himself (that was God Almighty), strong and resolute. He climbed onto the high gallows, brave in the sight of many, when he wished to redeem mankind.
I trembled when the warrior embraced me. Yet I did not dare to bow to the earth or fall to the corners of the ground. I had to stand firm.
I was raised up as a cross. I lifted up the mighty King, the Lord of the heavens; I did not dare to bend.
They drove dark nails through me. The wounds are visible on me, open wounds of malice. I did not dare to harm any of them.
They mocked us both together. I was all drenched with blood, poured from that man's side after he had sent forth his spirit.
Many cruel events have I endured on that hill. I saw the God of hosts severely stretched out.
Darkness had covered the Ruler's corpse with clouds, that bright radiance. Shadow went out, dark under the clouds. All creation wept and mourned the King's death. Christ was on the cross.
Yet eager ones came there from afar to the prince. I watched it all.
I was sorely troubled with sorrows, yet I bowed down to the hands of those men, humble, with great courage.
They took Almighty God there, lifted him from that heavy torment. The warriors left me standing, covered with moisture [or: blood]; I was all wounded with arrows.
They laid him down there, weary in limb, and stood at the head of his body. There they looked upon the Lord of heaven, and he rested there for a while, exhausted after the great struggle.
Then the men began to make him a tomb in the sight of his slayer; they carved it from bright stone, and set the Ruler of victories in it.
Then the wretched ones began to sing a song of sorrow for him in the evening, when they wished to go back, weary, from the glorious Prince. He rested there with a small company.
Yet we, weeping, stood there in our place a good while, after the voice of the warriors had gone up.
The corpse grew cold, the fair dwelling of life. Then someone began to fell us all to the earth. That was a terrible fate!
Someone buried us in a deep pit. But the Lord's thanes, his friends, found out about me there and adorned me with gold and silver.
Now you can hear, my dear man, that I have endured the deeds of evil people and grievous sorrows.
Now the time has come that people far and wide over the earth, and all this glorious creation, honor me and pray to this sign.
On me the Son of God suffered for a while. Therefore I now tower, glorious, under the heavens, and I can heal each one of those who stand in awe of me.
Long ago I became the hardest of punishments, most hateful to people, before I opened up for them, for those who have speech, the right way of life.
Listen! The Prince of glory, the Guardian of the kingdom of heaven, then honoured me above the trees of the forest!
In the same way, almighty God also honoured his mother, Mary herself, before all people and above all womankind.

Now I command you, my dear man, to tell people about this vision. Reveal in words that this is the tree of glory on which almighty God suffered for the many sins of mankind and for Adam's deeds of long ago.
He tasted death there. Yet the Lord rose again with his great power to help humankind.
Then he ascended into heaven. The Lord himself, almighty God, will come here again to this middle-earth to seek mankind on the Day of Judgement,
and his angels with him. Then he who has the power of judgement will judge each person according to what they have earned for themselves earlier, here in this passing life.
No one there can be unafraid because of the word that the Ruler will speak.
He will ask before the multitude where the man is who would taste bitter death for the Lord's name, as he did before on the cross.
But then they will be afraid, and few will know what they can begin to say to Christ.

But no one there who carries the best of signs in their heart will then need to be afraid. Through the cross, every soul that intends to live with the Ruler must seek the kingdom, away from the earthly road."
Then I prayed to the tree with a joyful heart and great zeal, where I was alone with little company. My spirit was eager for the journey onward. I have endured many times of longing in all.

Now my hope in life is that I may seek out the tree of victory, alone, more often than all other people, and honour it well. My desire for this is great in my heart, and I look to the cross for my protection.
I do not have many powerful friends on earth. They have gone on from here, from the joys of the world, and sought the King of glory. They live now in heaven with the high Father and dwell in glory,
and every day I look forward to the time when the Lord's cross, which I saw here on earth before, will fetch me from this passing life and then bring me to where there is great bliss,
joy in the heavens, where the Lord's people are seated at the feast, where there is everlasting bliss, and then set me where I may afterwards dwell in glory and fully enjoy delight with the saints.
May the Lord be a friend to me, he who suffered here on earth before, on the gallows-tree, for the sins of men.
He redeemed us and gave us life, a heavenly home. Hope was renewed, with glory and with bliss, for those who suffered burning there.
The Son was victorious on that journey, mighty and successful, when he came with a multitude, a host of spirits, into God's kingdom, the almighty Ruler,
to the joy of the angels and of all the saints who had dwelt in glory in the heavens before, when their Ruler, almighty God, came where his homeland was.
